thm:ucp-unit.title: UCP inverse theorem
thm:ucp-unit.note: Proved on a finite matrix factor Matrix d d C, the setting of the predictive channel monoid: a unital 2-positive map (complete positivity restricted to the M2 amplification, encoded blockwise via fromBlocks) with a 2-positive two-sided inverse is multiplicative, star-preserving and bijective. Kadison-Schwarz is derived from the block certificate [[1,a],[a*,a*a]] = B*B >= 0 and the Schur defect; squeezing through the inverse forces Schwarz equality for every element, and polarization of the sesquilinear defect upgrades it to full multiplicativity. The inverse needs only 2-positivity: its unitality and star-preservation are derived from the inverse identities. General finite-dimensional C*-algebras are direct sums of matrix factors; the statement is recorded at the factor level.

prop:radial-nonselection.note: Proved: for nonzero profiles A_s^0, B_s^0 with residues Z_Phi^0 = sum_s Tr(A^dagger A) and 4 Z_Omega^0 = sum_s Tr(B^dagger B), and every p in (0,1), the rescaled family A_s(p) = sqrt((1-p)/Z_Phi^0) A_s^0, B_s(p) = sqrt(p/Z_Omega^0) B_s^0 has Z_Phi(p) = 1-p and Z_Omega(p) = p, while the normalized profiles A_s(p)/sqrt(Z_Phi(p)) = A_s^0/sqrt(Z_Phi^0) (and likewise for B) are unchanged -- hence so are ranks and singular subspaces, which are functions of the normalized profiles. The stated normalization Z_Phi^0 + Z_Omega^0 = 1 is not needed for these identities and is omitted; positivity of the two residues (nonzero profiles) is the hypothesis used. The interpretation sentence is prose.
